scope.purpose: Identify original engine-facing functions that gameplay depends on, classify the boundary, and state the smallest modern interface OpenSpore needs without implementing it.
scope.target: SporeApp.exe 3.1.0.22, GOG x86:LE:32 PE, image base 0x00400000

sdk.name: Spore-ModAPI march2017 Ghidra XML
sdk.role: reference-only SDK names, signatures, structs, and enum semantics; no code or assets copied

analysis_snapshots.note: Live Ghidra includes thunk/external entries absent from the frozen pinned universe. Address-level conclusions use both, and SDK labels landing inside bodies are treated as anchors, not guaranteed entries.

method: CodeGraph exploration of current OpenSpore source and call paths before source inspection
Read committed SDK-boundary, reconstruction-readiness, RenderWare, Cell Stage, and replacement documents
Read Ghidra decompilation exports for named engine, Cell, resource, property, and RenderWare functions
Use live read-only Ghidra function lookup and xrefs for signatures, body ranges, caller totals, and vtable data
Cross-check committed SDK function anchors, probe definitions, asset-tool oracles, and current OpenSpore compatibility seams
Do not infer original runtime semantics from OpenSpore tests or implementation alone
excluded: modification of files other than this report

classification_vocabulary.required_for_semantics: The original function or boundary owns state, identity, ordering, event semantics, resource selection, or observable behavior that OpenSpore gameplay must preserve. The interface shape is part of the reconstruction contract.
classification_vocabulary.runtime_compatibility_only: The function is needed to reproduce host/application behavior or an event route, but its original implementation is not a gameplay semantic source of truth.
classification_vocabulary.replaceable_infrastructure: The original implementation is an engine service or storage/device mechanism that may be replaced by a modern equivalent while retaining its observable contract.
classification_vocabulary.renderware_third_party: The original function is RenderWare or another third-party/internal renderer implementation detail; preserve only the narrow semantic state or draw contract that gameplay can observe.
classification_vocabulary.os_runtime: Win32, CRT, input/audio device, timing, memory, or platform plumbing. Preserve the host contract, not the original platform call sequence.
classification_vocabulary.thin_wrapper: A getter, forwarding method, or small dispatch wrapper around a real service. It is useful for mapping ownership but must not be copied as a global singleton API into modern code.
classification_vocabulary.unknown: The body, layout, ownership, or meaning is not sufficiently characterized. The candidate interface is a placeholder for characterization, not an implementation prescription.

evidence_policy.sdk_name: Name-level provenance only; it establishes an SDK boundary anchor, not the truth of every decompiler type or field cast.
evidence_policy.ghidra: Static body, signature, vtable, and xref evidence. Decompilation is evidence-not-truth.
evidence_policy.xrefs: Direct-call, data, and vtable-reference counts are structural evidence of dependence, not proof of runtime execution.
evidence_policy.assets_and_tools: Real DBPF/GMDL/RW4/CellResource bytes and independent decoders establish content contracts and observed records; they do not establish original runtime field meanings.
evidence_policy.runtime_status: The committed evidence contains positive startup/menu evidence and negative or absent Cell-mode reachability. No claim in this report is promoted to runtime-observed Cell semantics.

summary.headline: Gameplay crosses a small set of semantic seams—mode lifecycle, shared game services, Cell state, content identity, and presentation—and a larger set of replaceable engine/runtime seams. The original global singleton and RenderWare/D3D internals should not become OpenSpore gameplay interfaces.
semantic_priority: Freeze mode and game-service contracts before reconstructing more gameplay functions.
Treat Cell state, player identity, world references, input/camera rays, and resource identity as semantic contracts.
Keep DBPF, GMDL, RW4, texture, Vulkan, SDL, and file/stream implementations behind narrow adapters.
Characterize the unnamed high-fan-in Simulator roots before assigning additional game semantics to them.
summary.important_negative: The current replacement status is replaced-approx, not live-runtime verified; 64/64 against the decompilation reference does not close the original ABI boundary.

boundaries.name: Application bootstrap and game-mode lifecycle
boundaries.why_gameplay_depends: A gameplay stage is entered, ticked, exited, and torn down through a virtual application/mode contract. The Cell stage's Initialize, OnEnter, and Update are explicitly part of the mode strategy rather than incidental engine calls.

minimal_modern_interface.name: IAppHost + IGameModeRegistry
operations: activateMode(unique_id) with old OnExit followed by new OnEnter
minimal_modern_interface.design_rule: Inject the host and mode registry into gameplay; do not reproduce the global DAT_015fd890 singleton or the original 27-slot ABI. Keep input callbacks on the mode interface, but model the modern event value as key, modifiers, mouse position, and wheel delta.

openspore_mapping.gap: The current host is a Cell executable, not a replacement for AppSystem/plugin bootstrap or the complete mode-manager service registry.

minimal_modern_interface.name: IGameServices
operations: input() returns normalized key/mouse/wheel state with event ordering
camera() returns viewer identity, projection/view state, and a view-ray provider
behavior() returns AI/behavior callbacks and event delivery
mode() returns the active mode identity and mode-transition operations
persistence() serializes gameplay state through the property/data boundary
clock().beginFrame() returns monotonic time, delta, and frame identity
minimal_modern_interface.design_rule: The original Get functions are accessors, not an API to reproduce. Keep service interfaces typed and injected; only the observable input, camera, behavior, persistence, and timing operations cross the boundary.

openspore_mapping.gap: OpenSpore has input, camera, and fixed simulation time, but not the original behavior, persistence, or service-root contracts.

minimal_modern_interface.name: ICellGameState + IEntityPool + ICameraRayProvider + IPlayerMovement

minimal_modern_interface.design_rule: Expose handles and typed gameplay state, not the original sCellGame offsets, DAT globals, or FUN helper names. Keep the real pool-index-to-entity relationship explicit; current POD replacement views are aliasing evidence, not a class-layout specification.

openspore_mapping.gap: The current pieces are not wired into a complete original-equivalent per-frame state machine. The current replacement status is replaced-approx and requires live Cell-mode evidence for promotion.

boundaries.why_gameplay_depends: Gameplay selects cells, worlds, populate records, effects, models, and textures by identity. The bytes and key selection are part of observable content behavior even though the original manager implementation is replaceable.

minimal_modern_interface.name: IContentStore + IRecordCodec
operations: read(RecordKey{type, group, instance}, ByteSpan) with explicit errors
read/write a named record through a versioned IRecordCodec
provide an IStream sink/source for streaming formats
minimal_modern_interface.design_rule: Keep the key triple and bytes at the boundary. Hide DBPF indexes, QFS, package priority, caches, and file paths. The existing B1 interface is the correct minimum: fetch by type/group/instance; extend it only for multi-package enumeration and priority when gameplay semantics require it.

openspore_mapping.gap: B1 currently serves one package image and reparses its index. The original multi-package search, cache/registry behavior, directory semantics, and load order remain unresolved.

The exact RenderWare implementation is not the gameplay contract, but the handles and resource associations are observable.

boundaries.why_gameplay_depends: Gameplay can observe which mesh/material/texture state is submitted, but should not depend on RenderWare object layouts, D3D vtables, or stream-cache internals. Preserve the semantic state sequence and replace the implementation.

minimal_modern_interface.name: IMeshDraw + IMaterialBindings + IGraphicsDevice

init/resize device, create render targets, beginFrame, present
minimal_modern_interface.design_rule: Model the state transitions, not the RenderWare object graph. The modern renderer may use Vulkan or another backend and may use its own descriptor/pipeline machinery, but gameplay-facing material IDs, texture slots, mesh topology, and draw ordering remain the compatibility surface.

openspore_mapping.gap: The current IRenderer has flat/textured mesh submission and a material approximation, but no full original shader/material/texture-slot contract or pixel oracle.

boundaries.name: Camera and input semantics at the stage boundary
boundaries.why_gameplay_depends: Mouse position, keyboard actions, camera mode, camera origin, and view direction directly determine movement targets and navigation. The event shell can be replaced, but the normalized values and camera-ray contract cannot be discarded.

openspore_mapping.gap: The current camera ray/plane model and input table are clean-room approximations; no successful original Cell trace has pinned camera state, pointer causality, or event ordering.

boundaries.name: Windows, CRT, input/audio device, and timing runtime
boundaries.why_gameplay_depends: The original depends on platform event delivery, time, file/memory operations, and optional audio/input devices. Gameplay may depend on normalized event/time/audio values, but not on Win32 or D3D implementation details.

minimal_modern_interface.name: IPlatformHost + IAudioSink
minimal_modern_interface.design_rule: Use SDL, Vulkan, and the host filesystem as adapters. Preserve event order, monotonic timing, and cue identity; do not preserve Win32 message IDs, DSOUND, DINPUT8, CRT wrappers, or registry/config plumbing.

openspore_mapping.gap: The current runtime path supports SDL3 presentation and deterministic fixed-step simulation, but original timing, audio, and input-device semantics are not live-observed.

minimal_modern_interface.name: blocked interface freeze
candidate_ports: IServiceLocator: named service handles, not raw global addresses
IPlayerIdentity: stable player handle and current mode identity
IObjectRegistry: object handle lookup and ownership/lifetime
IWorldState: current world/advect references and per-world state
IEventRouter: message-handler registration and ordered dispatch
minimal_modern_interface.status: Do not merge these candidate ports into one concrete interface yet. Characterize each root's body, returned global, and side effects first. The current OpenSpore interfaces must continue to use typed local state rather than guessed aliases.

openspore_mapping.gap: This is the first reverse-engineering blocker before broader Simulator gameplay reconstruction. It is intentionally a characterization target, not an implementation boundary.

deferred_or_non_boundaries.item: RenderWare/D3D9 device objects and vtable calls
deferred_or_non_boundaries.decision: Replace with the modern graphics device and draw-state interfaces in B-K-06. Preserve only state ordering, material/raster identity, and observable draw results.

deferred_or_non_boundaries.item: Full RenderWare RW4 model, skin, skeleton, blend-shape, and shader payload emulation
deferred_or_non_boundaries.decision: Keep the container contract behind the asset layer. Current structural RW4/GMDL support is narrow and not a reason to expose RW object layouts to gameplay.

deferred_or_non_boundaries.item: Full ResourceManager cache, directory, and multi-package load-order behavior
deferred_or_non_boundaries.decision: Required for broader content semantics but not yet an interface. A menu-transition trace and multi-package evidence are still needed.

deferred_or_non_boundaries.item: Full AppSystem/plugin bootstrap and UTFWin/editor hierarchy
deferred_or_non_boundaries.decision: Keep only event, mode, and service contracts unless the product scope expands to the original editor/UI.
Defunct service and explicitly non-goal; use a stub or omit it. It must not become a gameplay semantic interface.
Characterize before assigning semantics. Do not use OpenSpore's current approximations to backfill the original meanings.

recommended_interface_freeze_order.action: Decompile/export and characterize the ten unnamed high-fan-in roots plus map_int_whatever_find; record returned globals, signatures, and side effects.
Freeze mode lifecycle, service access, input/camera, behavior, persistence, and frame-clock ports using current IGameMode/CellInput/CellSim contracts.
Freeze Cell state/entity/resource identity contracts and distinguish content bytes from original manager/cache behavior.
Freeze Cell presentation world/layer/resource associations and camera-ray/input values; keep RenderWare implementation outside gameplay.
Keep modern renderer, event loop, property/codec, and platform adapters narrow. Add fields only when an original semantic or asset/tool differential requires them.

conclusion.result: Engine-boundary analysis completed without implementation. The highest-value semantic boundaries are the mode/game-service contracts, Cell state and movement state, content identity, Cell presentation world/resource bindings, and camera/input values. RenderWare and Windows/D3D details are replaceable implementation surfaces; singleton getters are wrappers, and the unnamed high-fan-in Simulator roots remain an explicit unknown requiring characterization.
conclusion.promotion_rule: No boundary claim in this report changes replacement status. Live Cell-mode evidence is still required before runtime-verifying the Cell ABI or original runtime ordering.
